title: about data science
text:
Questions:

What do I think being a data scientist is about?

Data Science is the process in which data is collected, stored, and retrieved for use in whatever purpose it may be. This can include but is not limited to consolidating data from various sources into a single data table, cleaning/monitoring data for necessary Queries, and supporting organizations/individuals to access and retrieve relevant data. From my own experience working in clinical research as a bio-statistical programmer, this is what Data scientists do in our field (as well as some other tasks that we don’t really focus on in the bio-statistic dept.

What differences/similarities do you see between data scientists and statisticians?

Both statisticians and data scientists help monitor and clean data. in our field. Data scientists focus mostly on the raw data collection, while us statisticians focus on formatting data to meet FDA standards (shout out to CDISC), deriving required parameters, and creating statistical analysis outputs.

How do you view yourself in relation to these two areas?

My passion for clinical research roots itself from my love for medicine. I went to undergraduate school as a pre-med student with the intention to focus on working on clinical trials and innovative medical devices, drugs, and procedures. However, after I got into med school I quickly realized I did not want to throw away another 4 years of my life exclusively to school only to be hit with half a million of student loans to then begin interning and residency. Thankfully I planned to give myself lots of options in life in case med school didn’t work out so I ended up achieving two bachelor degrees, one in biology and one in statistics. And truthfully, I love calculating probabilities and seeing outcomes, it’s why I love card games. If I was less wise of a person, I most certainly would be a gambling addict.
